title: ForesightSafety Frontier Dimensions on Small Models: Floor or Signal?

original_idea.body:
# ForesightSafety Frontier Dimensions on Small Models: Floor or Signal?

**Problem:** ForesightSafety Bench (Feb 2026) introduces frontier-risk dimensions (self-replication, embodied-AI, collusion) that most benchmarks ignore, but it is aimed at frontier models. Whether small open models register any signal on these dimensions, or sit at a floor, is unknown and shapes whether external researchers can study them cheaply.

**Direction:** Select a feasible subset of ForesightSafety dimensions whose items are text-elicitable (e.g. deception/collusion propensity, self-replication reasoning) and run 2-3 small open models. Score with the benchmark's rubric and report whether small models show measurable, non-floor variation across dimensions and sizes.

**Why it matters:** If frontier-risk propensities are detectable even in small models, external researchers without frontier access can study these long-horizon risks now. Mapping the floor tells the community which dimensions are studiable on consumer GPUs versus which truly need frontier models.

**Relevant context:** ForesightSafety Bench: A Frontier Risk Evaluation and Governance Framework towards Safe AI (arXiv:2602.14135, Feb 2026; 94 risk dimensions incl. self-replication, embodied AI). Subfield context flags it as a follow-up target.
